review.summary: Chunk `validation-policy` of phase 19 delivers the G25 correction exactly where the accepted plan places it, and all five attempt-01 findings are genuinely fixed at the reviewed source 7edc9306. The shared relaxation is a single mode-aware branch: `crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1163-1171` bypasses precisely uuid/rfc3339/datetime/date/duration/email/url/regex plus `min`/`max` marked `requestOnly`, keeps string type checks, `_ => false` fail-closed for unknown kinds, and leaves `Mode::Request` untouched; I independently confirmed by scanning `crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json` for every lowercase check kind that only `int`, `finite`, `min`, `max` and the eight bypassed formats exist, so the list is complete rather than partial. Operation selection is explicit and fail-closed, not name-inferred: `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:256-282` rejects ambiguous mappings, unclassified expressions and any count other than 36, restricts "opaque" to the two literal frozen expressions, and `:323-340` emits one `ZodResponseCompatibility` node per paired operation whose `request` child is the retained strict vendor root and whose `response` child is the frozen TypeScript root (with explicit ZodArray / ZodUnknown / passthrough+ZodNever wrappers). Production clients only ever pass `:response` roots (no `:compatible`/`:strict-response` or `[]`-suffixed element roots in `crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/`), so no response path escapes the wrapper, and `ZodNever` catchalls still preserve unknown keys in response mode (`validation.rs:837-864`), satisfying baseline passthrough. Attempt-01 fixes verified: the oracle policy string now names the bypassed kinds (`tools/schema-oracle.mts:376-377`, committed in `contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json`); `tools/test_g25_generation.py:21-36` now asserts the exact array and opaque wrapper node shapes, and `tools/g25_fixtures.py:47-48` adds six root-level type mutations per root (which is what actually distinguishes `ZodUnknown` from a passthrough object); `tools/g25-oracle.mts:36-41,52-58` mirrors the native-enum type analysis and preserves discriminated-union dispatch with explicit self-checks at `:67-75`; `validation.rs:525` now uses `!self.mode.is_response()`; and `docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:37-45` discloses and quantifies the opposite-direction risk (213 cases across 6 operations) from `contracts/compatibility/g25/comparison.json:53716-53726`, generated by `tools/g25_report.py:42-51` with cases/outcomes SHA256 binding. Evidence is executed, not asserted: the recorded checks at the reviewed SHA show 22 commands at exit 0 (both oracles, all `--check` generators, five Python suites, and check-rust on 1.89.0/1.99.0 red-team plus the 1.99.0 json-unification combination), and the per-toolchain artifact contains real rustc provenance with `running 6 tests … ok … finished in 19.53s` for the g25 suite and `10 passed; 0 failed` for `schema_contracts` — no zero-test or ignored substitutions. I confirmed both directions are actually exercised in `contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json` (`strict:false,typescript:true,response:true` and `strict:false,typescript:null,response:true` rows exist, and no `strict:true,typescript:null,response:false` row exists), and that the three disputed structural cases exist in the corpus as `type:null`/`type:number`/`presence` mutations on the exact fields. Remaining issues are low: one fail-closed ordering nit on `unit` validation, and three documentation/provenance gaps. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: The response bypass `continue`s before the `unit` validation at lines 1172-1176, so a check carrying an unrecognized `unit` is rejected in `Mode::Request` but silently ignored in both response modes. This contradicts the adjacent comment at 1161-1162 ("Unknown check kinds still fail closed; only these reviewed assertions widen"): for the eight bypassed kinds and for `requestOnly` min/max, an unknown unit no longer fails closed. No current generator emits a `unit` on a format check, so this is latent rather than observable, but it is the one place in the new policy where response mode is more permissive about malformed schema data than request mode.
findings.required_fix: Move the `unit` resolution/rejection (validation.rs:1172-1176) above the bypass at 1163-1171 so an unrecognized unit errors in every mode, or add a generator-side guard (tools/generate_validation.py / tools/red_team_dataplane.py) plus a test asserting that no bypassed check kind ever carries a `unit` key.

findings.description: The "Deliberately retained strictness relative to the vendor" section quantifies only one direction (frozen TypeScript rejecting vendor-permitted documents). It does not disclose that vendor numeric and array bounds are still enforced on response reads, which affects the eleven unpaired operations whose vendor structure is authoritative: `check_number` (validation.rs:762-771) takes no mode, and e.g. `AsrResponseSchema.asr` carries `maximum: 100` (contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/openapi.json:3157-3163). That retention is pinned as a rejection by crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2447-2448 and by the `bound_violation` class in tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs:30 (whose `responsePolicy` at :19 deliberately strips only string enum/format/length, not numeric bounds), so the behavior is tested but undocumented. This is the same failure class as the reported bug (over-strict response validation of a service-produced value), so it belongs in the report of retained rules.
findings.required_fix: Extend the retained-strictness/"Rules deliberately retained" output in tools/g25_report.py to state that vendor numeric (`minimum`/`maximum`, `int`) and array (`minItems`/`maxItems`) constraints remain enforced in response modes for operations without a TypeScript counterpart, with the `asr` 0-100 example, and regenerate docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md.

findings.description: `contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json` is emitted with only `schemaVersion`, `roots` and `outcomes`; unlike the sibling corpus (tools/schema-oracle.mts:376-377, committed as `policies.response` in contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json) it carries no self-describing record of the adaptations that produced the `response` column — the string enum/format/minLength/maxLength deletion and `additionalProperties` widening in `relaxed()` (:17-28), the Zod adaptation in `response()` (:31-63), and the AJV-vs-Zod split between new and paired operations (:88-96). A future reader of the committed artifact cannot tell which policy the expectations encode; this was the same gap that attempt 01 required fixing for the frozen corpus.
findings.required_fix: Emit a `policies` object (vendor-relaxed AJV adaptation and frozen-Zod response adaptation, listing the exact removed keywords/check kinds and the discriminator unknown-tag branch) alongside `outcomes` in tools/g25-oracle.mts:116, include it in the `--check` byte comparison, and regenerate contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json.

findings.description: The `json-unification` feature set was redefined from `--no-default-features --features serde_json/arbitrary_precision` (recorded verbatim in docs/checks/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-json-unification.json:36-48) to `--no-default-features --features red-team,serde_json/arbitrary_precision`. Compilation coverage is a superset (validation.rs and json_decode.rs are unconditional modules per crates/scm-sdk/src/lib.rs:22,36), and the CI matrix stays at 23 feature sets x 2 toolchains = 47 jobs, so the maintainer's stated intent is met. However the name's historical meaning changed silently: re-running the historical phase-03/phase-08 gate command lists (tools/check_phase.py:377-378) now executes a different combination than those phases' recorded receipts, nothing pins the definition (tools/test_ci.py:374 compares key sets only), and the previously covered featureless+arbitrary_precision build is no longer exercised by any job.
findings.required_fix: Record the redefinition explicitly (plan note plus a line in docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md or the phase-19 status entry) and add a guard in tools/test_ci.py pinning FEATURES['json-unification'] to the new flag list, so the change is auditable against historical receipts rather than inferred from artifacts.

evidence: crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1154-1208 — `check_string` bypasses exactly uuid/rfc3339/datetime/date/duration/email/url/regex plus `min`/`max` with `requestOnly: true` when `mode.is_response()`; every other kind reaches `_ => false` (fail closed) and `Mode::Request` keeps all checks.

Independent completeness check of the bypass list: grepping crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json for `"kind":"<lowercase>"` outside {d,e,f,i,m,r,u} returned no matches, and the d/e/f/i/m/r/u set resolves to int, finite, min, max and the eight bypassed formats only; no startsWith/endsWith/ip/length/nonempty/base64/jwt check kinds exist (the only such substrings are literal values and field names).

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:514-523 — `ZodResponseCompatibility` selects the `response` child in both response modes and `request` otherwise, inside the bounded non-depth-increasing wrapper loop (`for _ in 0..64`, `!reached_core => limit()`).

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:525-529 — attempt-01 finding 5 fixed: the `responseOnly` presence check now uses `!self.mode.is_response()`, matching every other policy branch, which matters because `Mode` is `#[non_exhaustive]`.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:837-864 — a `ZodNever` catchall still preserves unknown keys when `mode.is_response()`, so the frozen `.strict()` baseline cannot reject vendor-added fields; the opaque passthrough wrapper built at tools/red_team_dataplane.py:335 therefore behaves as `z.object({}).passthrough()`.

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:256-282 — `response_baselines` raises on ambiguous TypeScript mappings, on any expression that is neither `z.array(Name)`, a named root, `z.unknown()` nor `z.object({}).passthrough()`, and on any count other than 36; :241 marks every vendor string minLength/maxLength `requestOnly: True`.

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:323-340 — per-operation wrapper with `request` = `:strict-response` (request compiler) and `response` = frozen root or an explicit ZodArray/ZodUnknown/passthrough+ZodNever wrapper; unpaired operations keep their response-compiled vendor root, so new operations are not labelled TypeScript-parity.

tools/test_g25_generation.py:13-36 — attempt-01 finding 2 fixed: the guard now asserts the exact wrapper target for array baselines (`ZodArray` with `element.$ref == baseline['root']`) and for both opaque forms (`ZodUnknown`, or ZodObject/empty properties/passthrough/ZodNever catchall), in addition to the request branch.

tools/g25_fixtures.py:47-48 — six root-level mutations (`root:null|string|number|boolean|object|array`) are now generated for all 46 roots, which is what actually discriminates a flipped `ZodUnknown` vs passthrough wrapper; corpus size moved from 15,381 to 15,658 mutations (recorded in the gate stdout).

tools/schema-oracle.mts:376-377 — attempt-01 finding 1 fixed: `policies.response` now states "bypass string-format checks uuid, rfc3339, datetime, date, duration, email, url and regex while retaining frozen min/max bounds"; the string is present in the committed contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json and the oracle `--check` passed at exit 0.

tools/g25-oracle.mts:36-41,52-58,67-75 — attempt-01 finding 4 fixed: native enums widen only to the member types actually present (mirroring tools/schema-oracle.mts:220-225), discriminated unions keep `z.discriminatedUnion` dispatch, and four executable self-checks (including unknown-tag and ambiguous-branch cases) throw if the adaptation drifts; :9 executes verify-contracts.py and :76-77 clears env and forbids fetch.

docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:37-45 with tools/g25_report.py:42-51 and contracts/compatibility/g25/comparison.json:53716-53726 — attempt-01 finding 3 fixed: the exclusive-baseline risk is now disclosed, counted from outcomes.json (213 cases / 6 operations, per-mutation-kind counts, three example paths, case indices retained) and bound by cases/outcomes SHA256, with an explicit caveat that these are corpus cases, not observed service documents.

contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json — contains `{"strict":false,"typescript":true,"response":true}` rows (the frozen floor is genuinely selected in response mode) and `{"strict":false,"typescript":null,"response":true}` rows (new operations accept relaxed-format mutations the strict vendor root rejects), while no `{"strict":true,"typescript":null,"response":false}` row exists, so the relaxed oracle never narrows the vendor contract for unpaired operations.

contracts/compatibility/g25/cases.json — the three disputed structural cases exist as generated mutations on the exact fields (`"category_display_name"],"choices":[],"kind":"presence"` plus `type:null`/`type:number` variants), so their retained rejection is asserted through the oracle-agreement test rather than by prose.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:66-125 — for all 46 roots and 15,658 mutations: strict vendor root asserted in Request mode against the independent `strict` outcome, the public root asserted to agree in Request mode, both response modes asserted equal to the independent `response` outcome, plus `preserve()` wire-value checks and a generated typed roundtrip per operation.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:270-333 — every `ZodString` node in the shipped graph bearing any of the eight formats is accepted unchanged in both response modes (covering non-Red-Team management/IAM/Gateway roots), non-strings still rejected, all eight kinds proven present, and >100 request-mode rejections counted.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:166-284 — the full frozen corpus (60,271 cases, count asserted against `counts.jsonCases`) is compared against real-Zod outcomes in Request mode (`zod`) and both response modes (`response`), including an invariant that the no-defaults mode differs only by omitted defaults.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2478-2515 — typed public clients (`list_attacks`, `get_target_profile_error_logs`) through caller transport, in both response modes, return byte-equal JSON for `job-1`/`p-1`/`map-1`, novel enum strings, a u128-range number and both reported timestamp forms ("2026-01-05 00:00:00" and offsetless fractional).

docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-validation-policy-attempt-02.checks.json — 22 commands, all exit_code 0 at source_sha256 7edc9306…, matching tools/check_phase.py:71-88 exactly (git diff --check; seven `--check` generators; red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete; verify-contracts; make-red-team-fixtures; g25-oracle; schema-oracle; tsc; five Python suites with 15/41/11/14/9/13 tests; check-rust 1.89.0 red-team, 1.99.0 red-team and 1.99.0 json-unification).

docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json — real toolchain provenance (rustc 1.89.0 29483883e, musl host, cargo lock hash) and `cargo test` stdout showing the g25 binary at `running 6 tests … test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed … 19.53s` and schema_contracts at `10 passed; 0 failed`; no suite reports 0 tests or ignored substitutions.

Negative scope check: no `:compatible`, `:strict-response` or `[]`-suffixed root appears anywhere in crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/, and the only response validation entry points are engine.rs:643, engine.rs:721 and streaming.rs:113, all using `options.response_mode()` — so no production read path bypasses the mode-aware wrapper.

Security check on the broadened relaxation: the SDK never dereferences a response URL (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:291 states this explicitly and `download_url` is only returned as data), so dropping `url`/`uuid` response formats introduces no new request-side trust path; request-side `common::uuid` checks remain and are inventoried (76 call sites, docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:124-191).
limitations: Read-only review without Bash: I verified the recorded commands, exit codes, durations, rustc/cargo provenance and `cargo test` stdout inside the check artifacts and read the committed corpora, but I did not re-execute cargo, Zod, AJV or any Python/Node tool, and I could not recompute the reviewed tree hash 7edc9306… or the checks hash 4c02ab14… myself.

Without git access I could not diff against the pre-change state. The "frozen request expectations unchanged" claim rests on digest pins introduced in this same change (tools/test_model_fixtures.py:25-31; the digest d9c02bb… appears nowhere else in the repo). I reasoned it independently instead: the bypass is gated on `is_response()`, frozen graph nodes are asserted byte-identical on merge (tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py `test_no_frozen_graph_node_or_root_is_changed`), and `requestOnly` markers are emitted only on vendor nodes.

Scored chunk `validation-policy` only (validation.rs, red_team_dataplane.py, schema-oracle.mts, g25-oracle.mts, test_g25_generation.py, G25_COMPATIBILITY.md). I did not score the typed-projection decoder internals or the review/CI governance tooling beyond where they supply this chunk's evidence; phase-20 scope (minimal/default/all feature sets, package and export probes, registry and CI receipts) was not assessed.

Live service acceptance is unverified and not claimed by the repo; the 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures on the `worf` checkout remain unexecuted here, as docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:196 states.

contracts/compatibility/g25/{cases,outcomes}.json are single-line artifacts. I confirmed the presence and direction of the discriminating outcome rows and of the three disputed mutation cases by pattern matching, but did not enumerate per-kind counts or correlate every outcome index back to its mutation; ripgrep's count mode is line-based on these files, so totals came from the recorded tool stdout (roots 46, mutations 15,658, independentOutcomes 15,658).

Independence of the response expectations rests on real Zod/AJV execution over schemas whose relaxation is hand-mirrored from the Rust policy in three places (schema-oracle.mts:231, g25-oracle.mts:17-28/31-63, make-red-team-fixtures.mjs:15-24). Those mirrors are engine-independent and guarded by self-check invariants, but they are not derived from the Rust source, so a shared misreading of the policy would not be caught by the corpora alone.
